title: crosscutting-procedures-and-forms-2025
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview:
This document collates company-wide, cross-functional procedures and the canonical set of operational templates used at Redwood Inference. It is intended as the single-entry reference for: access & permissions, change management, data handling, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policy, and reusable internal templates. Use the procedures as written for standard cases; escalate to the listed owners for exceptions.

Quick navigation (by section):
- Access & Permissions (section 1)
- Change Management (section 2)
- Data Management (section 3)
- Procurement & Expenses (section 4)
- Vendor Management (section 5)
- Travel Policy (section 6)
- Templates & Forms (section 7)
- Roles, SLAs, and Escalation (section 8)

1) Access & Permissions
Intro: Access decisions balance least-privilege security with developer velocity. This section standardizes request flows, review cadence, and deprovisioning timelines.
Principles:
- Principle of least privilege applied to all systems.
- Access must be justified with business purpose and owner approval.
- Time-bound access where possible; automated expiry recommended.
Procedures (standard request):
1. Requester completes the Access Request Form (template A1). Include justification, duration, and systems.
2. Request goes to resource owner and security reviewer via ServiceNow (or current ticketing system).
3. Owner approves or requests changes within 48 hours.
4. On approval, IT/Platform grants access using the approved role profile and documents the grant in the ticket.
5. Automated audits run monthly; any stale access (>90 days unused) triggers owner review.
Sudo/Privileged access:
- Requires manager + security approval and completion of privileged-access training.
- Session recordings or audit hooks must be enabled for production environments.
Deprovisioning:
- Offboarding: deprovision in 24 hours of termination notification.
- Role change: adjust entitlements within 3 business days.
Audit thresholds (table):
- Monthly access review: owners must attest to 100% coverage.
- Stale access remediation window: 30 days from identification.
Example JSON payload (access request) for automation:
{"requester":"jane.doe@redwood.com","systems":["redwood-console","s3-customer-logs"],"roles":["read-only","billing-view"],"duration_days":14,"justification":"Support billing investigation for ACME"}

2) Change Management
Scope: Applies to platform services, production-facing infra, and any customer-impacting configuration or model rollout.
Change categories:
- Standard: pre-approved, low-risk (routine config changes).
- Minor: implemented during a maintenance window; requires owner sign-off.
- Major: impactful (schema migrations, model-swaps, infra topology changes) — requires CAB review.
Process:
1. Initiate a Change Request (CR) using template C1. Include rollback plan, test plan, and monitoring hooks.
2. Triage: change coordinator assigns category within 1 business day.
3. For Minor/Major: schedule a pre-change runbook review and run a dry-run in staging.
4. Approvals: Minor needs owner + SRE approval; Major requires CAB approval (see CAB roster).
5. Execution: follow the runbook, enable increased monitoring, and validate post-change health checks (SLOs).
6. Postmortem: if the change causes degradation, produce a 72-hour incident analysis and remediate.
Emergency changes:
- Must be clearly labeled and post-factum reviewed by CAB within 48 hours.
Change windows and blackout periods:
- Critical production changes allowed Monday–Thursday 01:00–04:00 UTC unless emergency.

3) Data Management
Categories: customer data, model artifacts, telemetry, aggregated analytics.
Retention policy (summary):
- Customer PII: retain per contract; default 90 days unless contract/region requires otherwise.
- Model artifacts and weights: retained per versioning policy; keep last 10 production versions plus stable archived artifacts.
- Telemetry: short-term hot storage 30 days, cold storage 2 years, aggregated metrics 5 years.
Handling rules:
- Encryption at rest and in transit for customer and model artifacts.
- Access to PII requires explicit approval and data handling training.
- Data minimization: collect only fields required for the purpose stated.
Data change procedure:
1. Submit Data Change Request with schema diff and migration plan.
2. Run migration in staging and verify with the canonical validation suite.
3. Schedule migration with rollback and monitoring.
Audit & retention controls table (text):
- PII deletion SLA: 48 hours from verified request (subject to legal holds).
- Backup verification cadence: weekly checks, quarterly restore drills.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Thresholds and approvals:
- Purchases <$5,000: manager approval.
- $5,000–$50,000: manager + finance approval.
- >$50,000 or multi-year commitments: procurement + legal sign-off + executive sponsor.
Expense reimbursement:
- Use Expense Template E1 and submit within 30 days. Attach receipts and card statements.
- Per diem and travel: follow Travel Policy (section 6).
Vendor onboarding checklist (abbreviated):
- Vendor risk assessment completed (template V-RA).
- Contract approved by Legal with data and IP clauses.
- Security questionnaire completed and reviewed by Security.
- PO issued and finance coded to the correct cost center.
Procurement SLA:
- Standard SaaS procurement: 15 business days from complete request to signed PO.
- Hardware orders: lead times vary; procurement will post expected delivery dates in ticket.

5) Vendor Management
Classification:
- Strategic: high-value, long-term partners; quarterly business reviews required.
- Tactical: replaceable services; annual review.
- One-off: ad-hoc, short-term vendors; sign-off by manager only.
Ongoing checks:
- Security posture re-evaluation every 12 months for Strategic vendors.
- Contract renewals: begin negotiation 90 days prior to expiry.
Escalation for vendor incidents:
1. Notify Vendor Manager and Legal within 2 hours for any PII/security incident.
2. Execute vendor incident runbook and coordinate customer notifications if required.

6) Travel Policy (summary)
Purpose: Reasonable, cost-conscious travel that supports business outcomes.
Booking rules:
- Use approved vendor for flights and hotels; upgrade rules require manager approval.
- Economy class for flights <8 hours; premium economy or business requires pre-approval.
Per diem and expense caps:
- Domestic per diem: $75/day for meals.
- International: country-specific caps (use Travel Template T1).
Safety & security:
- Register travel for overnight trips in the travel registry.
- Emergency contact: Global Security on-call; notify People Ops for health or safety incidents.
Travel approval flow:
1. Create travel request with purpose and estimated cost.
2. Manager approves and finance verifies budget.
3. Book through travel portal and retain receipts for reimbursement.

7) Templates & Forms (catalog)
- Template A1 — Access Request Form (fields: requester, systems, roles, duration_days, justification).
- Template C1 — Change Request (fields: owner, category, impact, rollback_plan, test_plan).
- Template D1 — Data Change / Migration Plan (schema diff, validation tests, data volume estimate).
- Template E1 — Expense/Reimbursement (amount, vendor, receipts, cost center).
- Template V-RA — Vendor Risk Assessment (security posture, compliance, data flows).
- Template T1 — Travel Request (trip dates, purpose, estimated cost, emergency contacts).
Templates are attached in the Confluence page attachments and versioned; use the latest version and embed the template ID in your request tickets.
Example: Access Request subject line — [A1] Access: jane.doe@redwood.com -> redwood-console (billing-view, 14d)

8) Roles, SLAs, and Escalation
Ownership matrix (text):
- People Ops: access governance, travel policy steward, offboarding execution.
- Security: privileged access review, vendor security questionnaires.
- Finance & Procurement: purchase approvals, vendor payments.
- SRE/Platform: change coordination, production runbooks, monitoring hooks.
SLA commitments:
- Access request initial triage: 2 business days.
- Deprovisioning after termination: 24 hours.
- Procurement turnaround for standard SaaS: 15 business days.
Escalation path (quick):
1. Owner -> Manager
2. Manager -> Function Lead (People Ops / Security / Finance / SRE)
3. Function Lead -> COO (for unresolved escalations beyond 5 business days)

Governance & review cadence:
- Annual policy review cycle owned by People Ops with stakeholders from Security, Finance, and SRE.
- Quarterly tabletop exercises for offboarding and vendor incident responses.

Appendices:
A. Contact list (text): People Ops mailbox: people-ops@redwood.com; Security on-call: +1-555-0102; Procurement: procurement@redwood.com.
B. Change Advisory Board (CAB) roster link: /confluence/eng-platform/cab-roster
C. Templates attachment notes: each template contains a change log and effective date in the header.

How to request an exception:
- Submit Exception Request (template EX1) to People Ops and Security. Include business rationale, impacted systems, and mitigation plan. Exceptions are time-boxed and require a renewal every 6 months.
